chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurarah who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The most beloved time to Allah, Exalted and Glorious, is its beginning, when the time for prayer enters. So pray the obligatory prayer. And if you do not do so, then you are in one of its times until the sun sets.'

key_terms.حِينَ يَدْخُلُ وَقْتُ الصَّلَاةِ: When the time for prayer enters

ai.seo_question: What is the best time to perform the obligatory prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) emphasizes that the most beloved time to Allah is the very beginning of the prayer window, establishing the principle of *Fadilat al-Awwal* (preference for the first time). This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that while delaying until sunset remains valid, it forfeits the spiritual merit of punctuality, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the distinction between the 'beginning' and 'end' of prayer times.
